population.note: FICTIONAL. Of ~273M adults: current 17.4% ≈ 47.5M, ever 28.6% ≈ 78.1M, used-and-off-now 11.2% ≈ 30.6M, never ≈ 195M. Cycling: ≈8.6 pts of current users are on a second or later course and ≈4.0 pts of the off-now group restarted at least once and stopped again, so (8.6+4.0)/28.6 = 44%. That fits ~33% one-year persistence in weight-coded commercial plans (employer drops add involuntary stops), ~50% in diabetes-coded and Medicare plans, and 40–50% restart within a year through $149–199 orals, the free FQHC programme and imports. Ever-use rose 4.6 pts (≈12.6M new first starts), and ≈8.8 pts of current users are on a first course. Age check: 18–29 10.5% × 52M = 5.5M; 30–49 19.5% × 90M = 17.6M; 50–64 28.5% × 61M = 17.4M; 65+ 10.2% × 70M = 7.1M; total ≈ 47.5M ≈ 17.4%. The 18–29 band rose most (7.5→10.5) because the Mar 2032 vaping/smoking-cessation approval brings $0 preventive coverage, and normalisation reaches people who were never heavy. The 65+ band rose only 1.7 pts because of bone pauses and, since Aug 2032, heat-season advice. Income: the bottom third rose 10.3→14.7 through Medicaid, the Community Incretin Program (≈1.5M, almost all bottom third) and ≈5.1M import users, who are under-measured. The middle third barely moved (15.0→16.0) because employer retreat lands hardest there. Its incomes are too high for the FQHC programme, and many people find $199/month cash a stretch. The top third (21.5%) pays cash without noticing. Of the ≈30.6M off now, an estimated ~6M lost weight-coded employer coverage in 2031–32, ~3M are on DEXA- or clinician-advised pauses, and the rest stopped for side effects, cost, 'the grey' or conviction. Pediatric: 0.9% of ~73M under-18s ≈ 660k: ≈540k adolescents 12–17 and ≈120k children 6–11 after the Mar 2031 approval. Roughly three in ten US children live with at least one parent currently on a drug. No child has more than ~9 years of exposure, and interim adolescent bone-accrual data (2032) are inconclusive.

access.public_coverage: Medicare: the $199 rate, $50 copay, BMI/comorbidity criteria and counselling visit are extended through Dec 2032 unchanged, with renewal talks for 2033 entangled in the generic cliff. Medicare pays 16% of fills ≈ 7.6M users (≈6.8M aged 65+ plus ≈0.8M disabled under-65), of whom ≈2.2M use the Bridge successor for obesity: 2.2M × $199 × 12 ≈ $5.3B in 2032. Medicaid pays 10% ≈ 4.75M users at $199: 4.75M × $199 × 12 ≈ $11.3B gross federal+state before supplemental rebates. Indiana and Arkansas waivers are unchanged. New: the Community Incretin Program, created by the Safe Incretin Access Act (Nov 2031), gives oral semaglutide free through FQHCs and state health departments to uninsured or underinsured adults with BMI ≥35, or ≥30 plus a comorbidity. HHS buys all oral strengths at a flat $149. Enrolment is ≈1.52M at end-2032 (3.2% of fills). 2032 spend is ≈1.2M average × $149 × 12 ≈ $2.15B against a $3.0B/yr appropriation; the end-year run-rate is 1.52M × $149 × 12 ≈ $2.7B. The programme does not gate on outcomes and requires only a monthly pharmacist check. Also new: after the Mar 2032 smoking-cessation approval, ACA §2713 tobacco-cessation preventive rules require non-grandfathered plans and expansion Medicaid to cover cessation courses at $0. Plans may limit this to two 12-week courses a year and require a prior NRT or varenicline attempt.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India: 100+ semaglutide brands, including generic 25–50 mg oral tablets at $4–25/month. China: domestic generic semaglutide and tirzepatide-analogue pens, and Chinese API underlies most of the gray trade. Canada: generic semaglutide CAD 50–80/month, and a generic oral launched in 2031. Brazil, Mexico, Turkey and the Gulf have generics. US: settlements with ANDA filers set licensed generic semaglutide entry for 2033, pushed back six months by the pediatric exclusivity earned with the Mar 2031 under-12 approval. No US generic exists at end-2032.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Managed decline holds. Federal direct-pricing portal (launched as TrumpRx): oral starting doses $149; Wegovy pill 50 mg $199 from launch (Jun 2031); injectable semaglutide $199; tirzepatide $199–249; retatrutide direct cut from $399 to $299 (Dec 2031); amycretin direct $299; survodutide $279. List prices are unchanged (Wegovy $1,349, retatrutide $1,499) and almost nobody pays them. PBM net ≈$160–180. Payer mix of ≈47.5M users: commercial 38% (18.05M: ≈8.5M weight-coded, ≈7.8M diabetes/cardiac/OSA/CKD/MASH-coded, ≈1.75M cessation-coded at $0), Medicare 16% (7.6M), Medicaid 10% (4.75M), Community Incretin Program 3.2% (1.52M), cash/direct 22% (10.45M, including ≈1.2M 'calm' subscribers), imported/counterfeit 10.8% (5.13M) = 100%, ≈47.5M. Employer weight-management coverage fell from 63% to 51% of employers. Of those still covering, ~75% gate (≥80% PDC, verified weigh-ins, ≥5% at 6 months). Coverage is now concentrated on diabetes, cardiovascular, OSA and cessation codes, and prediabetes 'code creep' is a PBM audit target. Orals were ≈55% of 2032 new starts. The 503B exclusion and 503A injunction stand. Personal importation is still not legal but is not prosecuted against buyers.

on_market_classes: GLP-1 agonist, weekly injectable (semaglutide: Wegovy/Ozempic, incl. 7.2 mg)
GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GLP-1 + amylin analogue combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema)
GLP-1/amylin unimolecular co-agonist, weekly injectable (amycretin, approved Mar 2031)
GLP-1/glucagon dual agonist, weekly injectable (survodutide, approved Dec 2031 after resubmission)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill incl. 50 mg high dose, 2031; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: MASH / liver (semaglutide; survodutide label includes MASH data)
smoking and vaping cessation in adults (oral semaglutide, Mar 2032; 12-week courses, anhedonia Warning and Precaution)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: adolescent vaping cessation (16–17), widely prescribed off-label after the adult approval
low-dose 'calm'/'even' subscriptions, now smaller and relabelled 'dose-light' after FTC consent orders
'metabolic health' / longevity regimens in concierge practices
prediabetes-coded prescribing to retain coverage after employer retreat
gambling and compulsive-shopping craving reduction, still anecdotal
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. The oral-parity driver is realised as a line extension of an existing product, not a new molecule. Wegovy pill 50 mg (sNDA, approved Jun 2031) was non-inferior to weekly injectable semaglutide 2.4 mg in a 72-week head-to-head (−16.4% vs −16.9%), with a DEXA substudy as the 2029 bone guidance requires. It matches the most-used injectable but not tirzepatide or retatrutide. The real needle barrier fell for the semaglutide tier. Oral amycretin is in phase 3 (readout 2032, filing planned 2033) and is not on the US market. Amycretin (subcutaneous) was approved Mar 2031 after 72-week DEXA data. Survodutide was approved Dec 2031 with a lean-mass/heart-rate label. FDA extended MariTide (filed Apr 2030) to demand 72-week DEXA, and a decision is now expected 2033. Bimagrumab combinations remain in phase 3, with filing announced for late 2032. The semaglutide smoking-cessation sNDA was resubmitted Aug 2031 with a 26-week trial using SHAPS and C-SSRS endpoints (continuous abstinence 34% vs 19% placebo; clinically meaningful anhedonia 6% vs 2%) and approved Mar 2032 for oral semaglutide only. Pediatric 6–11 approval (STEP Young-type 68-week data, −12% BMI vs placebo) earned six months' pediatric exclusivity. Incretin market ≈$131B in 2032: US volume up ~20%, US net flat to −5%, ex-US eroding. Analysts model a US semaglutide net-price fall of 40–60% in 2033.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of voluntary discontinuation. High-dose oral (50 mg) has GI rates similar to injectables. Unsupervised escalation of imported tablets adds ED visits.
Elevated with rapid loss; retatrutide and survodutide users contribute more cases.
No causal confirmation; absolute risk low. Counterfeit-product cases still confound reporting.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; MDL litigation ongoing, with bellwether trials scheduled 2033.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Population problem beyond 65+. Lean loss is ~30–40% of weight lost in untrained users over 50. Survodutide's label carries lean-mass language.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class label (2028) and the 2029 joint guidance retained. FDA now cites 72-week DEXA as standard (amycretin, MariTide).

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Hip/vertebral fracture HR ~1.3–1.4 in 65+ long-term users and ~1.2 in postmenopausal women 50–64 who cycle. With ≈3M 65+ users on >2 years, that is ~6,000 excess hip fractures a year. DEXA waits have eased to 4–6 weeks as capacity grew.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class labelling and DEXA guidance retained. The DOJ civil case from the HELP referral is unresolved.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Cohorts still conflict; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA 'very rare' label; FDA warnings mention; no class determination.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: The cessation trial's C-SSRS data showed no excess.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: The warning, removed Jan 2026, has not returned.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('the grey', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Upgraded from emerging. The randomised cessation trial found clinically meaningful SHAPS anhedonia in 6% vs 2% placebo at 1.4–25 mg oral equivalents. Retatrutide observational data show ~10–14% at top doses. Mostly reversible within 4–8 weeks of stopping or a dose cut.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: First label language: a Warning and Precaution for anhedonia and reduced reward on the cessation indication, with class-wide labelling requested for 2033. FTC consent orders (2031) with two 'calm' brands bar focus and anxiety claims.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Employer retreat added a wave of involuntary stops in Jan 2031 and Jan 2032 plan years. Regain is visible within months, and many people switch to cash orals or imports instead.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly. EEOC technical assistance (Feb 2031) warns that gates penalising medically advised pauses may violate the ADA. The Indiana waiver case is still pending in the Seventh Circuit.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Iron, B12, vitamin D, calcium and protein signals persist in high-loss and older users, and now in some pediatric users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Professional guidance (2029) retained. AAP 2031 guidance adds growth and nutrition monitoring for under-12s.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~7 years; adolescent exposure; repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About ten years of follow-up for the earliest users. Interim adolescent bone-accrual data (2032) show slightly lower BMD accrual than BMI-matched controls, still within normal range, and are inconclusive. No data yet exist for under-12s.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Postmarketing requirements; the 6–11 approval carries a 10-year growth, puberty and bone registry requirement.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination, substitution)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: The flood moved to pills. A spring 2031 cluster of counterfeit 'Wegovy pill' blister packs containing sibutramine caused ≈90 cardiac ED visits and 2 deaths (CA, NV, IL). Poison-centre incretin calls are up ~60% over 2030. Vial mg/unit errors and Chinese-sourced endotoxin cases continue.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Safe Incretin Access Act (Nov 2031): felony penalties for selling counterfeit incretins, CBP/FDA funding for parcel screening, and mandatory serialised pen and blister authentication. Buyers are still not prosecuted, and personal importation is still not legalised.

safety_ledger.effect: Falls and frailty-related injury in older users
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Fall-related ED visits remain elevated in 65+ users with >2 years' use. Part may now be attributed to the volume-contraction signal (orthostasis) below.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: In the 2029 joint guidance; the CMS counselling template includes fall-risk screening.

safety_ledger.effect: Blunted thirst (hypodipsia) with chronic low-grade volume contraction: kidney stones and heat-related acute kidney injury after 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: NEW and unforeseen. A Kaiser Permanente/VA analysis (Jul 2032) of ≈190k users with ≥5 years' continuous use finds a nephrolithiasis HR ~1.3 rising with duration (none detectable below 2 years) and a heat-related AKI hospitalisation HR ~1.6 in users 65+ during the summer 2031 heat events in Phoenix, Las Vegas and the Central Valley. A metabolic substudy finds ~250–350 mL/day lower 24-hour urine volume and blunted thirst ratings on osmotic challenge, consistent with rodent work on GLP-1 and fluid intake. With an estimated ~3.5M continuous ≥5-year users nationally, ~0.4%/yr baseline stone incidence × 0.3 ≈ 4,000 excess stones a year; heat AKI excess is in the hundreds to low thousands. This does not contradict FLOW-type CKD protection, and nephrologists argue publicly about how both can be true. Diuretic and SGLT2 co-use confound it.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA Drug Safety Communication (Aug 2032); a label update is under negotiation. CDC heat-health guidance now lists long-term GLP-1 users alongside diuretic users. The AUA advises 24-hour urine testing after a first stone. No restriction on use.

food_and_beverage.state: US salty-snack and confectionery volume is down another ~2–3% a year. Kids' snack lines face their first measurable pressure in high-uptake suburbs after the 6–11 approval. Protein, fibre and 'bone-forward' claims are standard. The fastest new line since August 2032 is 'hydration for GLP-1 users': electrolyte drinks, flavoured waters and timed-reminder bottles, with one sports-drink brand running 'Thirst Is Optional, Water Isn't' ads. Pill users report slightly more grazing than weekly injectors, and single-serve 'pill-day' packs exploit that. The 'real food, full portion' heritage brands are flat.

alcohol.state: Spirits post a fifth straight year of US volume decline, and beer is down in the 25–40 male segment. 'Calm' subscriptions shrank after the FTC orders, which slightly slowed the loss of occasional drinkers. The bigger story is tobacco: after the Mar 2032 cessation approval and $0 coverage, US cigarette volume is running ~−11% annualised against ~−8% before, and disposable-vape sell-through to 18–29s is down sharply. Tobacco majors guide to faster declines and lean on nicotine pouches.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat and spend per cover is still down in high-uptake suburbs. Half portions, by-the-gram protein bowls and kids' 'small plates' are standard. Chains in Phoenix and Las Vegas push free water refills and electrolyte add-ons. Atlanta's and Memphis's 'no-gram' rooms survive, but they are now one niche among many rather than a movement.

apparel.state: Size churn continues in both directions. Coverage-loss regain in Jan 2031 and Jan 2032 drove a visible January surge in larger sizes. Children's sizing is shifting slowly in affluent districts. Plus-size specialists are stable.

fitness.state: Still growing, but more slowly. Employer retreat cut some corporate wellness budgets. Medicare Advantage strength benefits and DEXA-plus-coaching chains keep expanding, and DEXA capacity has mostly caught up. Summer outdoor programmes in the Southwest now build in hydration checks.

insurance.state: Employer weight-management coverage fell from 63% to 51% over 2031–32 plan years. The reasons were the EEOC's ADA guidance on gating and medical pauses, fracture and now kidney claims in cost models, the existence of $149–199 cash orals and a free public programme, and a wait for the 2033 generic cliff. Coverage concentrated on diabetes, cardiac, OSA, CKD and cessation codes, and PBMs audit prediabetes code creep. The $0 cessation mandate is an unplanned cost line: ≈1.75M commercial members, two 12-week courses a year. Pharmacy trend is ~+4%.

pharma.state: US volume is up ~20% over the window and net price is flat to slightly down. Novo partly recovers on Wegovy pill 50 mg, the cessation and pediatric approvals and the federal programme's oral contract, while preparing for 2033 generic semaglutide. Lilly still leads by revenue with tirzepatide, retatrutide and Foundayo, and faces new competition from amycretin and survodutide. Authentication and serialisation vendors grow under the 2031 Act's mandate. Generic makers holding settled 2033 entry dates are building US capacity.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Being on it is unremarkable. In insured suburbs and in most workplaces nobody asks, much as nobody asks about statins. Being off is what needs explaining, and there are now accepted explanations: 'my DEXA', 'my plan dropped it in January', 'I did my twelve weeks for vaping', and in Phoenix since August, 'my kidney doctor'. 'Off by conviction' is still a recognised reading, but a smaller one. Visible January regain reads as coverage loss, not failure. Resistance-trained shoulders still mark doing it right, and a water bottle has become a long-term user's accessory.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: The tiers have hardened. The top third (21.5%) pays cash for retatrutide or amycretin with DEXA and coaching. The bottom third (14.7%) gets oral semaglutide free at the health centre, on Medicaid, or from India by mail. The middle third (16.0%) lost employer plans and pays $199 a month cash or goes without, and middle-income suburbs of Dallas, Charlotte and Columbus show the widest on/off mix. In Houston and Phoenix, people still ask whether a pill or pen came 'from the portal' or 'from the mail'.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Meals are smaller and protein-first by default, and children's birthday parties now plan for kids on semaglutide. Sunday dinners and church potlucks persist but are rarely framed as resistance any more. The old three-group holiday planning (on, off, off-by-conviction) has settled into 'on' and 'whoever's on a break'.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Profiles still list on/off, but filtering on it has declined among under-40s, for whom being on is assumed. 'Unmedicated' survives as an identity filter in religious and body-sovereignty communities. Advice columns have moved from 'my partner is too calm' to negotiating a shared dose-holiday schedule.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is medicalised and mostly depoliticised. The free FQHC programme split the 2030 coalition. Some Atlanta wellness collectives now run peer-support groups inside health centres, while others call the programme 'pharma on the public dime'. Tulsa–Dallas congregations still preach appetite as a gift, with smaller audiences. Berberine sellers pivoted to 'natural hydration' supplements after the kidney signal. Refusing the drug is now a minority practice rather than a movement.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. The randomised cessation trial puts clinically meaningful anhedonia at ~6% vs 2% placebo on oral semaglutide, now on the label. Observational retatrutide data put it at ~10–14% of top-dose users. A 2032 KFF-style poll finds ~38% of current users say the drug 'dulls things I used to enjoy' at least sometimes, and ~33% took at least one planned dose holiday in the past year. Pharmacology shapes the practice: Foundayo's short half-life makes weekend holidays workable, semaglutide's roughly week-long half-life means skipping one dose, and gated plans' 80% PDC rule caps holidays at roughly two weeks a quarter. The ≈1.2M 'dose-light' subscribers are unmeasured.
interior_life.framing: Now a recognised side effect rather than a product feature. 'The grey' is common speech and appears in the cessation label as 'anhedonia and reduced reward'. Clinicians ask about it at refills, and 'have you tried a holiday?' is routine advice. Wellness brands that sold the effect as 'Quiet' now sell 'dose-light' plans with 'adjustable calm', under FTC orders that bar focus and anxiety claims.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Dose management is a workplace norm. Sales, hospitality and creative workers cut doses before peaks, and some managers schedule around colleagues' holidays without saying so. Fleets and call centres still favour steady use, and DOT-related tirzepatide use continues. With weight coverage gone at many employers, the work link shifted from adherence surveillance to the benefits office explaining that the cessation course is free and weight treatment is not. Tech-firm lifestyle accounts still reimburse dose-light plans at some firms.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Written unmedicated' still sells in Nashville, but the bigger trend is 'holiday sets'. Touring comics and DJs schedule weekend shows for audiences on dose breaks, and some Las Vegas promoters market 'off-week' weekends. Critics now routinely ask whether a flat record is 'the grey', and some artists publish their dosing schedules. Intense stimulus such as hot sauce, loud rooms and extreme sport remains popular among users.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Sex therapists screen for dose and for cessation courses, since a 12-week vaping course can flatten a relationship's first months. Couples coordinate holidays, and 'Saturday off' is an established phrase. Backlash framings of the drug as a threat to marriage have faded outside religious communities.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: It is about cost, coverage and safety, not temperament. The Safe Incretin Access Act passed as 'seal the mail, open the clinic', a bipartisan trade of counterfeit penalties for free provision. The 2032 campaign argued over whether to extend the programme to the middle third before generics arrive. The kidney signal reached Arizona and Nevada races as a heat-policy issue. Campaigns still privately test 'calm voter' messaging, and no turnout effect is established.

state.regulatory_posture: FDA is still data-demanding (72-week DEXA as standard, the MariTide extension) but approved the long-delayed cessation and pediatric 6–11 indications and three new obesity products, which signals that the bone pause is over but scrutiny is not. FDA issued a Drug Safety Communication on the kidney/heat signal. The FTC enforces advertising claims through consent orders. The EEOC has entered the field through ADA guidance on outcome gating. The Safe Incretin Access Act (Nov 2031) is the first new statute in the area.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: Direct subsidy: the Community Incretin Program gives oral semaglutide free to ≈1.52M uninsured and underinsured adults through FQHCs and state health departments. HHS buys at a flat $149, with a $3.0B/yr appropriation through FY2034 (2032 spend ≈$2.15B). Effective mandate: ACA preventive rules require $0 coverage of the cessation indication (two 12-week courses a year, step therapy allowed). Medicare stays at $199 with a $50 copay. There is no mandate for weight treatment, and private coverage for it is shrinking.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Conditioning is diverging. The Indiana and Arkansas waivers are unchanged (≥80% PDC, quarterly verified weigh-ins, two misses = 12 months off). The federal programme deliberately does not gate on outcomes, needing only a monthly pharmacist check and an annual weight. Gated employer plans shrank with employer retreat but remain ~75% of those still covering. The 2031 Act's serialisation requires each pen and blister to be scanned at dispensing, which creates a national dispensing log that privacy advocates have begun to question.
state.workforce_or_military: DOT sleep-apnea screening still makes tirzepatide a de facto job requirement for some drivers, and some fleets add hydration and heat protocols for long-term users in Southwest routes. Army accession policy on GLP-1 use is still contested. A 2032 DoD pilot accepts recruits stable on oral therapy for ≥6 months, with a waiver.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: China's API and India's finished tablets dominate the gray trade, which has shifted to pills that are easier to mail. The Act funds CBP screening, and seizures are up, but import users still rose to ≈5.1M. A 2032 India–US trade framework includes an Indian commitment on export labelling and serialisation, with no legalisation of personal importation. Section 232 tariffs remain. Generic makers with 2033 US entry dates are building domestic fill-finish to claim capacity credits.

events.event: EEOC issues technical assistance warning that employer GLP-1 coverage rules which end benefits after doctor-ordered DEXA pauses may violate the ADA; within months several Fortune 100 employers announce they will drop weight-management coverage for 2032 while keeping diabetes, cardiac and sleep-apnea codes, and the share of employers covering falls toward 51%

FDA approves semaglutide injection for obesity in children aged 6 to 11, with a 10-year growth, puberty and bone registry; the approval grants six months of pediatric exclusivity that pushes settled US generic entry into 2033

FDA approves a 50 mg Wegovy pill after a 72-week head-to-head trial shows it matches weekly injectable semaglutide (−16.4% vs −16.9%); Novo prices it at $199 on the federal portal, and by 2032 pills are more than half of new starts
events.driver: next_gen_launch: oral_parity; price_path: managed_decline; cultural_response: normalisation

events.event: After counterfeit 'Wegovy pill' blister packs laced with sibutramine are tied to about 90 cardiac ER visits and two deaths, Congress passes the Safe Incretin Access Act: felony penalties for counterfeit sellers, mandatory serialisation, and a $3 billion-a-year Community Incretin Program giving free oral semaglutide through health centres to uninsured adults

FDA approves oral semaglutide for smoking and vaping cessation with the first label warning for 'anhedonia and reduced reward'; ACA preventive rules make 12-week courses free in most plans, and 'the grey' becomes a refill-counter conversation

A Kaiser Permanente–VA study of 190,000 people on GLP-1 drugs continuously for five years or more finds blunted thirst, more kidney stones and a 1.6-fold rise in heat-related kidney injury among older users during the 2031 Southwest heat waves; FDA issues a Drug Safety Communication in August

open_tensions: The 2033 semaglutide generic cliff is close. Employers have already left weight coverage, Medicare's $199 rate expires Dec 2032 without a successor, and the federal programme buys at brand $149. Nobody has decided who captures the price fall when generics arrive, or whether the middle third, now the least served, gets anything before then.

The kidney/heat signal falls on the longest-term, most adherent users, exactly the people that gated plans, Medicaid waivers and Medicare's continuity rules reward. Advice to pause in summer or after a stone can trip the 80% adherence rules that remain in Indiana, Arkansas and ~75% of covering employers.

The $0 cessation mandate is now the widest door to free coverage. Plans see 'smoker coding' and fight it with step therapy, while the cessation label is the one place anhedonia is formally warned about. A free 12-week course of a drug with a reward-blunting warning is going to 18–29-year-olds at scale.

About 120,000 children under 12 and 540,000 adolescents are on semaglutide, in a culture where being on is normal and three in ten children live with a parent on it. Inconclusive adolescent bone data, no under-12 data, and a new effect that only appears after five years mean the children who start now are the cohort that will reveal the next unforeseen effect.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide is sold in the US; first licensed entry is now settled for 2033.
Wegovy's list price remains $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
Oral starting doses (Wegovy pill, Foundayo) are still $149–150 a month cash through the federal direct-pricing portal (launched as TrumpRx) and manufacturer direct channels.

The Indiana and Arkansas Medicaid 1115 waivers still require ≥80% proportion-of-days-covered and quarterly verified weigh-ins; two misses end coverage for 12 months, and the disability-rights litigation is still unresolved in the Seventh Circuit.
The suicidal-ideation warning removed from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels in January 2026 has not returned; the cessation trial's C-SSRS data showed no excess.

prose.headline: The Pill Won, the Plan Left: One in Six Americans Is On It Now, and Some of Them Have Stopped Feeling Thirsty
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2032 about one American adult in six is on an incretin drug, and nobody remarks on it. In most offices and suburbs being on it is the background condition, like a statin. People who are off are the ones asked to explain, and they have stock answers: a scan, a plan that dropped it in January, a twelve-week vaping course that ended, a kidney doctor.

The needle stopped mattering in June 2031, when a 50-milligram Wegovy pill matched the weekly injection in a head-to-head trial and went on sale for $199 on the federal portal. It was not a new molecule, and it did not beat tirzepatide or the triple agonists the wealthy use. But it erased the last reason most people had for waiting, and pills became more than half of new starts.

The employers left at the same moment. In February 2031 the EEOC warned that coverage rules ending benefits after a doctor-ordered bone-scan pause might violate disability law. Faced with either removing the gates or removing the benefit, large employers began removing the benefit. Coverage for weight alone fell from nearly two-thirds of employers to about half. What stayed was coverage for diabetes, heart disease, sleep apnoea, and from March 2032 smoking. The country now has two kinds of patient: those who carry a qualifying code and those who carry a credit card.

Washington, which had passed nothing for years, passed something. A spring cluster of counterfeit pills cut with sibutramine killed two people and produced the bargain its sponsors called 'seal the mail, open the clinic'. The Safe Incretin Access Act made selling fake pens and pills a felony, required serial numbers on every blister, and funded a Community Incretin Program that gives oral semaglutide free through health centres. About a million and a half uninsured adults use it, at roughly $2 billion this year. The programme does not weigh anyone against a threshold. The people it misses are in the middle: insured, newly uncovered, and earning too much for a health centre to treat them. About five million people still buy pills from India and China by post, because $199 a month is real money.

The FDA approved the two indications it had resisted. Children from six to eleven can now be prescribed semaglutide, under a ten-year registry. Adults can take it to quit cigarettes or vapes. The cessation label carries the first official warning about 'anhedonia and reduced reward', and under existing preventive-care law most plans must cover those courses at no cost. Young adults are the fastest-growing group of users, and cigarette sales are falling faster than they have in years. What the wellness brands sold as 'Quiet' is now a common complaint. A third of users take planned breaks, timed to concerts, anniversaries and the 80 percent adherence rules that still bind the remaining gated plans.

Then came the finding nobody had looked for. In July a study of people on the drugs continuously for five years or more found they drink less because they feel less thirst. They form more kidney stones, and in the 2031 Southwest heat waves older users were hospitalised with kidney injury at 1.6 times the expected rate. The numbers are small, a few thousand extra stones a year, and the same drugs protect diseased kidneys in trials. Nephrologists argue in print about how both can be true. CDC heat guidance now lists long-term users beside people on diuretics, and a sports-drink company has a new campaign.

None of it looks like a crisis. Snack volumes keep easing, spirits are down a fifth year, and gyms are full. The cheapest version of the most-used drug arrives as a generic in 2033. No one has decided who will get the savings, and the people who have used it longest are being told to drink water whether or not they feel thirsty.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Marisol Treviño's alarm goes at 5:10. She swallows the pill with a capful of water, exactly four ounces in the measuring cup by the sink, and does not eat or drink for thirty minutes. Outside it is already ninety-four.

The pharmacy app shows $199, approved. The dental group dropped the coverage in January. Ray's charge underneath reads $0.00: week nine of twelve, vaping.

She fills her mother's jug and draws hour lines on it in Sharpie. Lupe, seventy-one, seven years on the injection, passed the stone on Sunday. The urologist told her to drink. 'I'm never thirsty, mija,' Lupe says, 'that's the whole point.' Marisol sets the jug's reminder to buzz every ninety minutes.

At the practice, the hygienist's light shows her the third dry mouth of the morning. The patient, a roofer, asks if she's on. 'Everybody's on,' he says before she answers.

At lunch the pediatrician's office calls about Mateo, ten. The doctor wants to 'discuss the new option'. Marisol books it for after school starts, not before.

Ray is on the patio when she gets home, guitar case shut. 'Haven't wanted a hit in three weeks,' he says. 'Haven't wanted to play either.' The plan covers two courses a year. He says he'll stop at twelve and see which one comes back.

Dinner is chicken and beans in small bowls. Mateo asks for seconds and she gives them to him.

At ten the jug buzzes on Lupe's side of the duplex wall. Marisol listens until she hears the tap run.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Employer retreat added a wave of involuntary stops in Jan 2031 and Jan 2032 plan years.
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: the chain names the Feb 2031 EEOC guidance as the trigger, so it cannot cause a January 2031 wave of stops. Employers that remain keep gating at ~75%, up from ~70%, which cuts against the claim that ADA exposure drove the retreat.

least_plausible_claims.quote: The 18–29 band rose most (7.5→10.5) because the Mar 2032 vaping/smoking-cessation approval brings $0 preventive coverage, and normalisation reaches people who were never heavy.
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: the largest age-band jump, about 1.6M extra young users, is credited to an approval only about nine months old at end-2032. Preventive-coverage rules and 12-week courses would not plausibly ramp that fast, and no earlier young-adult driver is shown.

least_plausible_claims.quote: With an estimated ~3.5M continuous ≥5-year users nationally, ~0.4%/yr baseline stone incidence × 0.3 ≈ 4,000 excess stones a year
least_plausible_claims.why: magnitude: 3.5M users with five unbroken years looks too large against the stated ~33–50% one-year persistence and ~44% cycling. It sits close to the 3M 65+ users on more than two years, so the headline excess-stone count rests on a shaky base.

rationale.badness: This is a recognisably harder society with new losers, not a collapse. The middle third is squeezed ('tiers have hardened', employer retreat), children are on the drugs with inconclusive bone data, anhedonia is on a free cessation course going to 18–29s, and a new kidney/heat signal falls on the most adherent users. Offsets are the free programme, less gating coercion, falling smoking and harms that are named, measured and labelled, which keeps epistemic and autonomy scores moderate. Inequality is highest because of the on-code-or-credit-card split.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: every driver is visible in fields and events. Adoption is +2.8 to 17.4%. Employer coverage fell 63→51%, the 6–11 and cessation approvals and the 50 mg pill (a line extension) are all in, as are the counterfeit pills, the Safe Incretin Access Act subsidy, the 'grey' as a labelled complaint, and the kidney/thirst signal. mechanism: most chains are shown (EEOC to retreat, the Act, the cessation trial to label to coverage), but the Jan 2031 stops predate the Feb 2031 EEOC trigger, the 18–29 jump is attributed to a nine-month-old approval, and the new thirst effect arrives with a convenient substudy and a fast FDA response. magnitude: current, ever-use, income thirds, age bands, payer mix, the Medicare, Medicaid and CIP spend and pediatric counts all sit inside the envelope and multiply out. The only gaps are the inherited near-total overlap of Medicare 65+ (6.8M) with the 65+ band (7.1M) and the doubtful 3.5M continuous five-year users.

least_plausible_claims.quote: With an estimated ~3.5M continuous ≥5-year users nationally
least_plausible_claims.why: This fails magnitude and mechanism. With the parent world's ~33–35% one-year persistence, only a small fraction of pre-2027 starters could still be continuous 5+ years later. The figure also sits oddly beside a 190k-person study cohort and a 'none detectable below 2 years' finding drawn from a ≥5-year cohort.

rationale.badness: There are real new losers: a middle third that lost employer coverage and pays $199 cash, ~660k children on the drug, a reward-blunting label warning, and a new kidney/heat harm in the longest-term users.
